findings.observation: One recursive source gate protects acquire_checked/native owner-count/flag-or-predicate/unlock as one short operation. A separate short clock call protects frequency cache and QPF/QPC. Polling Sleep and observer calls occur after source guard release.
SourceGuard preserves Windows LastError around its lock/unlock operations. It leaves OS/Platform effects visible, while optional observer bookkeeping has its own PreserveError.

The new source guard never invents native unlock or rollback. Error5/error6 and overflow count adjustment remain before flag publication; a release exception retains flag/native count writes but emits no event. Unknown native outcomes are outside retry contract.

Eight own threads take800 clock samples through one wrapper; root quick result confirms one frequency query and coherent cache. Source gate excludes timer calls while native flag lock is held in the supported method paths.

A separate finisher thread completes while waiter Sleep is blocked under an independent test CV. Observer can wait for another Execution clock caller, proving source guard is released before observer invocation.

Exact flag addresses map Server/Online/Libraries; unrelated flag still receives recovered write but emits no event. Preseeded1 flags do not publish, duplicates cannot fill missing bits, aliased references/reused observer are rejected, and foreign issuer invalidates readiness.

Atomic acq_rel fetch_or events form an RMW synchronization chain; all-bits acquire makes ordinary payload writes before the three worker event releases visible. Core test reads payload after observed_all and before thread joins.

Host event is recorded only after normal host source return, before attachment completion. It is not engine success. Server event precedes async_accept/run_context and is not worker completion. Library/online events publish their completed initialization prefixes only.

Resources strongly retains Publication until after Execution destruction; matched foreign factory verifies exact CallbackStateView Execution identity. Execution is immovable and observer cannot be rebound/reset for another owner. By-value Resources consumers and Execution owners require complete rebuild.

coverage_notes.observer_production_contract: published is noexcept atomic bookkeeping; arbitrary observer callbacks that throw or violate lifetime are unsupported

limits: One Execution wrapper must own all concurrent access to its MutexState, flag references and frequency cache; raw helpers/outside plain mutation/second wrapper remain outside coverage
OS lock and QPC boundaries must be short, non-reentrant and follow nonthrowing native SDK contracts; recursive source mutex is not general provider-reentry support
An unexpected native lock/unlock/QPC exception does not gain retry or safe rollback semantics
Milestones publish initialization prefixes, not engine health, worker/FLS quiescence, joins, hook state or image unload
Remaining shared streams, provider state, fallback/OOM and foreign concurrency constraints still require explicit caller proof; milestones never activate callbacks from worker threads
Original CRT/native mutex ABI, native callback general overlap/reentry, external hooks and full DLL equivalence remain unproven
